message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm), the freezing point of pure water is **about –2 °C**.  

This value comes from the water phase diagram: as pressure falls below the normal atmospheric pressure, the ice–water equilibrium line slopes downward, so ice forms at a slightly lower temperature. At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is roughly –2 °C (the exact value can vary by a few tenths of a degree depending on purity and measurement conditions).
